an3.16:1.1: _Apaṇṇaka_ (“sure bet”) is a gambling term, where _paṇṇa_ appears as a form of the number five. While a hand of four dice was “perfect” (_kaṭa_), the fifth “losing” (_kali_) die was all-powerful, since just one extra die meant you lose everything (Rig Veda 10.34.2, Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 5.4.4.6). _Apaṇṇaka_ is therefore literally a “set without a fifth” and metaphorically a “sure bet”. See further note on [mn60:12.5]().
an3.16:1.3: These are three key practices in the ethics portion of the Gradual Training, intended as support for medititaion. For full details, see [dn2]().
an3.16:2.2: The “features and details” are aspects of what is seen that provoke desire or aversion, such as the “sign of beauty” in a person’s face, body, movement, or adornments.
an3.16:2.3: It is not that one cannot see things, but that, mindful of its effect, one avoids unnecessary stimulation. | “Covetousness and bitterness” (_abhijjhā domanassā_) are the strong forms of desire and aversion caused by lack of restraint.
